relevance_note: Single case report of a person with a clinical diagnosis of Alexander disease (in scope by diagnosis), but no GFAP testing: 'A five-year-old girl is presented as a case of juvenile Alexander disease'; 'genetic testing are not available in our setup'.
method_note: Built by hand with a short Python script; every value read from the paper. One in-scope person: the single unnamed patient (label 'patient'), diagnosed clinically from clinical, EEG and MRI findings; brain biopsy and GFAP testing were not available, so no variant is tied to her and the variants table is empty. n_patients_reported left null: the schema counts patients with a GFAP variant and none is described (0 tested); the paper describes 1 clinically diagnosed patient. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null (paper is silent). Parents ('non-consanguineous parents with no family history of neurological disorders') get no rows: not tested and not described as affected. Age at onset not given as an age: symptoms began 'four months ago' at age five; recorded as feature onset text only, with age_at_onset not reported. 'Normal birth and developmental history' before onset vs Discussion's 'psychomotor retardations' and regression: checklist 'developmental delay' left not reported (premorbid development stated normal; later loss is regression). 'Cognitive decline' left not reported although 'inability to understand' is listed among regressed milestones. 'Normal globi pallidi and thalami' is narrower than checklist 'basal ganglia or thalamic abnormality' (caudate/putamen not addressed), so that item is not reported; 'no ventriculomegaly' does not address hydrocephalus/raised ICP, left not reported. Periventricular T2 hyperintensity is not the T1/T2 'periventricular rim' sign, left not reported. Pseudobulbar palsy not mapped to dysphagia/dysarthria checklist items. 'Extensive neurometabolic analysis ... came up inconclusive' and 'no other positive findings' recorded as nothing. Normal head circumference recorded as excluded macrocephaly (D-27). No contradictions found.
